newsitem.title: INDIA: Nearly 70 pct of U.S. investment headed for W.India.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 70 pct of U.S. investment headed for W.India.

text.p: Western India is expected to attract $3.4 billion in U.S. investment, or 67 percent of the total projected American investment in India in the four years to 2001, Ambassador Frank Wisner said on Friday.
Wisner told a meeting of businessmen that Indian economic reforms had achieved much, but their potential could only be realised if policies were implemented.

"Our projections show that of the over $5,000 million of new investment expected from 1997 to 2001, western India will have the lion's share -- $3,369 million, or 67 percent of the total," Wisner told the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce.
Wisner said the figure had been generated by a recent U.S. Embassy study of American investment patterns in India.
He said the country's wealthiest state of Maharashtra had attracted between 30 and 45 percent of total U.S. investment in India despite its lengthy bureaucratic procedures.
"Of total U.S. investment in India of $1,339 million in India until the end of 1995, Maharashtra alone had captured $605 million, or 45.2 percent of the total," Wisner said.
He said the figure for industrialised western India -- including the states besides Maharashtra -- had dropped slightly in 1996 to 32 percent, or $135 million of the total of $425 million invested.

"The problem most often cited for Maharashtra was red tape, an incredible volume and variety of red tape," Wisner said, warning the businessmen that investors would choose to put their money in those states where it would bring results fastest.
He said two recent steps by India had given proof of the country's determination to revitalise its economy.
"India's most recent budget was welcome evidence of a national determination to build an economy based on modern, free-market principles, and to engage further global markets," Wisner said.
"So, too, was India's recent decision in the World Trade Organisation to sign the Information Technology Agreement," he said.
